name: Cedar shoe inserts

lead: Cedar inserts are wooden forms left in shoes between wears. They keep the shoe in shape and are said to absorb moisture and add a woody scent, leaving shoes and feet fresher.
Foot odour is attributed to bacteria acting on sweat, and proponents say the porous wood draws moisture out of the shoe. No studies on cedar for odour were found.

paras: People slip cedar trees into shoes after each wear, often alternating pairs and pairing them with sock and foot hygiene habits.
No harms are documented in the sources found.

angle.text: Users place cedar shoe trees in footwear between wearings to absorb moisture and add a woody scent, so shoes and feet smell fresher and shoes keep their shape. No trials on odour exist.

lead: Cedar shoe inserts are wooden pieces, often shaped like shoe trees, placed in footwear between wearings. A shoe tree is described generally as a device placed in a shoe to preserve its shape.[1] In appearance and grooming communities they are discussed as a way to limit foot and shoe odour, since cedar is commonly said to absorb moisture and carry its own scent.

Foot odour is generally attributed to sweat combined with bacterial activity, and general references list foot hygiene, sock choice and medicated insoles among prevention measures.[2] No source consulted for this entry examines cedar specifically.
infobox: Shape retention, moisture and odour control

paras: Shoe trees are placed inside a shoe to help it keep its shape.[1] Cedar versions are among those sold to enthusiasts of leather footwear, and are marketed on the basis that the wood takes up moisture and has a natural aroma.

Sweat itself is odourless; odour arises when bacteria on the skin and in closed shoes break down sweat and dead skin, with species such as Brevibacteria and Staphylococcus epidermidis implicated.[2] Closed, padded shoes trap moisture, and general references recommend daily sock changes and keeping feet dry.[2]

lore.intro: Cedar inserts are mentioned as a low-cost odour-control and shoe-care measure in grooming discussion.

claims.claim: Cedar absorbs moisture and odour from shoes
